t: Buddhism introduced to Korea from China
c: Buddhism, also one of the major religions in East Asia, was introduced into China during the Han dynasty from Nepal in the 1st century BC.

t: Yang Jian establishes Sui dynasty
c: In 581 AD, Yang Jian overthrew the Northern Zhou, and established the Sui dynasty.

t: Gung Ye deposed, Wang Geon raised to throne
c: In 918, Gung Ye was deposed by his own generals, and Wang Geon, the previous chief minister was raised to the throne.

t: Genghis Khan unites Mongol tribes
c: In the early 13th century Genghis Khan united warring Mongol tribes into the united Mongol Empire in 1206.

t: Mongol forces invade North China
c: From 1211, Mongol forces invaded North China.

t: Mongol Empire conquers Western Xia
c: In 1227 the Mongol Empire conquered Western Xia.

t: Ögedei Khan extinguishes Jin dynasty
c:
In 1234, Ogedei Khan extinguished the Jin dynasty.

Ögedei Khan was the second khan of the Mongol Empire.

t: Mongols begin invasion of Korea
c: In 1231, the Mongols began to invade Korea, and quickly captured all the territory of the Goryeo outside the southernmost tip.

t: Last Song remnants defeated at sea
c: The last remnants of the Song were defeated at sea in 1279.

t: Goryeo surrenders to Yuan as vassal state
c: By 1275, Goryeo had surrendered to the Yuan dynasty as a vassal.

t: Pi Sheng invents movable type system
c: The first known movable type system was invented in China around 1040 AD by Pi Sheng (spelled Bi Sheng in the Pinyin system).

t: Korea invents metal movable type
c: The world's first metal-based movable type was invented in Korea in 1234, 210 years before Johannes Gutenberg invented the printing press in Germany.

t: China and France fight war over Vietnam
c: In 1884–1885, China and France fought a war that resulted in China's accepting French control over their former tributary states in what is now Vietnam.

t: Japan annexes Ryukyu Kingdom as Okinawa
c: In 1879, Japan annexed the Ryukyu Kingdom, then a Chinese tributary state, and incorporated it as Okinawa prefecture.

t: Imperial examination system abolished in China
c: In 1905 the examination system itself was abolished and the entire Confucian tradition of merit entry into the elite collapsed.

t: Japan occupies Manchuria and founds Manchukuo
c: In 1931, Japan occupied Manchuria ("Dongbei") after the Manchurian Incident, and in 1937 it launched a full-scale invasion of China.

t: Japan invades French Indochina
c: Instead of withdrawing, Japan invaded French Indochina in 1940–41.

t: U.S., Britain, Netherlands cut off Japan oil imports
c: In response, the U.S., Britain and the Netherlands cut off oil imports in 1941, which accounted for over 90% of Japan's oil supply.

t: North Korea invades South Korea
c: In 1950, after years of mutual hostilities, North Korea invaded South Korea in an attempt to re-unify the peninsula under its communist rule.

t: Qing abolishes imperial examination system
c: The abolition of the examination system in 1905 marked the end of official Confucianism.

t: Northern Zhou conquers Northern Qi
c: During the late Northern and Southern dynasties period, the Xianbei-led Northern Zhou conquered the Northern Qi in 577, reunifying northern China.

t: Early Lý dynasty loses Hanoi to retaking forces
c: The Hanoi area formerly held by the Han and Jin dynasties was easily retaken from the Early Lý dynasty ruler Lý Phật Tử in 602.

c: Hostilities between the Tang and Tibet continued until they signed the Changqing Treaty in 821.

c: Upon its completion in 801, the map was 9.1 m (30 ft) in length and 10 m (33 ft) in height, mapped out on a grid scale of one inch equalling one hundred li.

t: Liao launches expedition against Northern Song
c: In 1004, the Liao launched an expedition against the Northern Song dynasty.

t: Jin dynasty destroys Liao dynasty
c: The Liao dynasty was destroyed by the Jurchen-led Jin dynasty in 1125 with the capture of the Emperor Tianzuo of Liao.

t: Emperor Taizong officially renames dynasty Great Liao
c: In 938 or 947 Abaoji's successor, Emperor Taizong of Liao, officially renamed the dynasty as Great Liao.

t: Emperor Daozong reintroduces Great Liao
c: In 1066 Emperor Daozong of Liao reintroduced the dynastic name Great Liao, and the title remained in official use until the dynasty's collapse.
